C-KERNEL-OPERABILITY-COMPATIBILITY-UPGRA.IntentSummary: Establish the operability, compatibility, and upgrade contracts for Worldline: machine-checkable Stable/Experimental contract lifecycle rules and SDK N/N-1/N-2 matrix; staged package upgrade with migration-on-copy, bounded pre-switch health validation, and atomic active-revision switch; LastKnownGood rollback with fresh runtime identity and authority isolation; persistent quarantine and security-preserving safe mode; bounded automated plugin bisect; per-runtime operational metrics without raw payload leakage; diagnostic causality reconstruction; explicit Incomplete side-effect outcomes; and property, fuzzing, negative-security, and process-kill chaos hardening suites.

T-001.Title: Inventory current interfaces and write ADR-OPERABILITY-COMPATIBILITY-UPGRADE-V1 including Cordis-rs lineage

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: ADR-OPERABILITY-COMPATIBILITY-UPGRADE-V1.md exists and covers all required sections: Contract stability model, Compatibility rules, Supported SDK/kernel matrix, Package revision model, Staged upgrade protocol, Migration-on-copy, Health validation, Atomic switch and rollback, Safe mode, Quarantine and bisect, Operational telemetry, Incomplete external outcomes, Replay boundaries, Cordis-rs lineage and deliberate divergence, Rejected alternatives, and Reopen conditions.

The ADR explicitly records that Cordis-rs lifecycle/effect ownership is architectural lineage, while external compatibility, upgrade transactionality, persistent package revisions, and crash rollback are Worldline contracts.

T-002.Title: Introduce contract stability, package revisions, and compatibility resolver in worldline-plugin-protocol

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: worldline-plugin-protocol defines PackageRevisionId, InstallationRevision, ContractStability (Stable, Experimental), and machine-readable CompatibilityMatrix rules.
Capability contract stability is metadata of a contract version line, not a provider self-declaration. Provider cannot self-declare Stable to bypass negotiation.
Compatibility evaluation is deterministic and machine-readable; no decisions based on filename or lexical guessing.
Versioned compatibility fixtures for SDK N, N-1, and N-2 are added under fixtures directory.

T-003.Title: Implement staged package revision storage without activation and compatibility resolver in kernel

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: worldline-kernel implements CompatibilityResolver evaluating provider capability declarations against required contracts under Stable/Experimental rules.
Staging a new package revision registers the revision metadata but grants NO active provider authority, publishes NO capability broker endpoints, and mutates no active installation state.
Incompatible major or unsupported experimental revision produces explicit CompatibilityRejected prior to activation.
State migration for upgrade executes against an isolated staged copy/snapshot of installation state.
Original state remains intact until new revision passes health validation and switch commits.
Migration provenance records source revision, target revision, source schema, target schema, migration path, and result.
Failed migration preserves current state and revision intact.

T-005.Title: Implement pre-switch health validation and probe execution

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Pre-switch health validation runs required checks: manifest and ABI compatibility, state migration success on copy, runtime activation, required capability publication, dependency resolution, bounded health probe (deadline and budget), and no immediate traps/crashes.
Passing health validation grants no additional authority.
Failed health validation preserves current revision and leaves active state unaltered.

T-006.Title: Implement durable atomic active-revision switch and crash recovery

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Switch has a single durable committed active-revision decision in storage.
Crash before switch recovers previous Current revision; crash after switch recovers new Current revision (or explicit rollback-required); never two authoritative Current revisions.
Capability broker never exposes both old and new revisions simultaneously under single-provider semantics.
New revision receives a fresh RuntimeId and inherits zero runtime grants from previous runtime.

T-007.Title: Implement LastKnownGood rollback and post-switch observation window

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: LastKnownGoodRevision is durably recorded and restored on rollback.
Rollback restores package revision, compatible state snapshot, and composition selection metadata.
Rollback creates fresh RuntimeId and fresh live authority; does not resurrect old handles or grants.
Post-switch observation window detects activation crashes, repeated restarts, required provider disappearance, health probe failures, and triggers automatic rollback according to policy.

T-008.Title: Implement persistent quarantine, safe mode, and bounded automated bisect

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Repeatedly broken plugins enter persistent quarantine with reason, sequence/timestamp, and originating revision; quarantined plugins do not auto-activate across host restart.
Quarantine preserves installation state and does not delete packages.
Safe mode boots a minimal known-good composition suppressing optional third-party plugins while strictly enforcing capability authorization.
Automated bisect isolates offending optional plugins over a bounded candidate set with outcomes LikelyCulprit, MultipleCandidates, or Inconclusive.

T-009.Title: Implement per-runtime operational metrics and diagnostic causality queries

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Operational metrics record activation/deactivation durations, restart/crash/hung/quarantine counts, RPC in-flight/queue depth, event mailbox depth/drops, authorization denials, memory/CPU usage without raw payload data.
Diagnostic causality query reconstructs ordered causal facts from correlation/causation metadata without timestamp guessing.
Missing or pruned causal evidence appears explicitly as a diagnostic gap.
Diagnostic query enforces caller permissions and never leaks payload data.

T-010.Title: Implement explicit Incomplete side-effect outcome and replay boundary policy

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: SideEffectOutcome defines NotStarted, CommittedLocal, Succeeded, Failed, and Incomplete.
Crash after external side-effect dispatch but before outcome acknowledgement yields Incomplete.
Incomplete is not treated as Failed or Succeeded, and is not automatically retried unless idempotency is verified.
Deterministic replay is restricted to explicitly designated event-sourced domains; other domains recover via authoritative stores.

T-011.Title: Add resolver and upgrade property tests

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Resolver properties verify determinism, incompatible provider rejection, irrelevant provider independence, authority separation from compatibility, and authority non-inheritance.
Upgrade properties verify single active revision invariant, pre-switch failure safety, and stale handle non-revival on rollback.

T-012.Title: Add negative security suite and fuzzing smoke suite

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Negative security suite tests cross-runtime handle reuse, revoked handle reuse, manifest self-grants, WASI escapes, ProviderSelf after replacement, state handle after rollback, and authority inheritance after upgrade.
Fuzzing smoke suite tests manifest parser, IPC envelopes, compatibility negotiation, and diagnostic causality query parser against arbitrary/malformed inputs without host panics.

T-013.Title: Implement process-kill chaos matrix in worldline-storage

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Storage failpoints cover staged migration, pre-switch validation, active switch commit, post-switch, rollback, and outbox recovery.
Hard process kills at each kill point recover into a fresh host process with exact single-revision assertions and no corrupted state.

T-014.Title: Integrate M0.7 verification into repository-owned CI and static architecture guard

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Invoke-WorldlineCi.ps1 suites Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, and ProvingSlice run all new compatibility, upgrade, property, negative-security, fuzzing, and chaos suites.

Test-WorldlineArchitecture.ps1 verifies that upgrade/compatibility code does not import browser/agent/UI domain types, safe mode has no product-specific branches, and diagnostics cannot bypass broker.

T-015.Title: Run full M0 regression and verify permanent proving slices

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: S0, S1, external-provider S1 proving paths, and staged upgrade proving scenarios run green.
Builtin, native-process, and WASM provider conformance remains green.
All M0 exit criteria from ROADMAP.md are proven by fresh evidence.

T-016.Title: Reconcile durable GRACE projections and close milestone M0 in ROADMAP

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: M-OPERABILITY-COMPATIBILITY-UPGRADE and V-M-OPERABILITY-COMPATIBILITY-UPGRADE are routed in graph and verification documents.
ROADMAP.md marks M0.7 Done and M0 Complete, and sets M1.1 Browser Contract and Engine Spike as Next.
Completion packet reports all required fields with explicit separation of scaffolded, wired, and verified evidence.
